correctness.rationale: The kernel is reconstructed from the two d-edge conditional averages, giving C[e,f]=(A[u,b]-A[a,v])/d². Counting the overlap of two d²-sized edge sets gives 2d−1+c4(e), whence exact row sums 2((d−1)²−c4(e))/d²; skew symmetry yields the L¹ norm and row-sign functions attain it. The extremal graph statement is secured by Hall-factorizing a projective-plane incidence graph; zero commutator forces every component to be K_{d,d}. On projective planes AA^T=qI+J gives principal-angle cosine sqrt(q)/(q+1), yielding the stated Hilbert norm. The stdlib checker extracted from the work package was actually run and produced ALL_CHECKS_OK 44523; finite tests corroborate but do not substitute for the universal proof.

value.rationale: The invariant measures order-sensitivity of two natural conditional least-squares averages on incidence-supported data. The exact universal four-cycle formula resolves it for every regular bipartite support, identifies both sharp max and zero cases, and provides an explicit high-degree family whose L² commutator vanishes while strong endpoints converge to the maximal difference-of-contractions scale 2. The sharp graph-structural classification is usable without computing matrix norms and goes beyond a small numerical or cosmetic instance.
